kind: actual Linux x86_64 source-coverage exports; focused re-check of the GH-259 generated-owner gap on the required compiler
runtime: real cargo test runs under -C instrument-coverage via cargo-llvm-cov; JSON format 3.1.0
purpose: Confirm whether the function-like proc-macro generated-owner gap persists on the required compiler, and test whether emitting the generated source into a real file yields distinct owners with a real zero record for an unexecuted function.

cases.name: proc-macro token stream (pinned fixture, default)
cases.note: Only the macro implementation and the two consumer test functions appear. The generated business functions have no function entry. This reproduces the recorded 1.97.1 gap on 1.98.1.

cases.name: proc-macro token stream (pinned fixture, branching)
cases.note: Same omission with the branching feature; visit_expr_if count changes 2 -> 3, confirming the feature actually selected different generated tokens.

cases.name: generated source placed in a real file and pulled in by include!
cases.fixture: ad hoc, same two-template generator shape
cases.note: When the generated source text is a real file brought into the crate, each generated function gets a distinct owner with real counters, and the deliberately unexecuted function gets an explicit zero record rather than being absent.

cases.name: generated source written by a build script into OUT_DIR and pulled in by include!
cases.note: Same result when the generated file is produced at build time and included by path, which matches how a build-time generator would share one generation path between the macro entry and the collector.

finding: The omission is not tied to the compiler version: Rust 1.98.1 with matching LLVM reproduces the 1.97.1 result for the token-stream macro. Distinct generated owners, including a real zero record for an unexecuted function, are obtainable on this same stable compiler when the generated source is a real file brought in by include! rather than only a proc-macro TokenStream.
scope_limits: This is a bounded two-template observation, not general macro support.
It does not certify generated-function coverage for the proc-macro path, which remains unsupported.
It does not compute CRAP; CRAP needs certified complexity and coverage identity for the same owner and an accepted migration.
Owner names above are demangled for readability; the raw exports use mangled symbols with source filenames.
Not cross-system acceptance and not a production-signature result.
Core thresholds, requiredness, baselines and historical evidence are unchanged.
next_actions: Submit the prepared upstream capability reports through a maintainer with issue-creation permission; the current token receives HTTP 403 on rust-lang/rust.

Decide with Core review whether a real-file generator path (shared generation library that also emits a bound source file) is an acceptable supported boundary for generated owners, before any metric promotion.
Keep generated proc-macro coverage and CRAP explicitly unsupported until a real mapping exists.
